name: BaByliss trimmers/stylers

lead: BaByliss makes hair dryers, straighteners, curling irons, clippers and beard trimmers. The brand began in France in 1960 and has been owned by Conair since 1995.
This entry is short because the available sources cover the company and general clipper design rather than specific products.

paras: Clippers and trimmers cut hair with two close-fitting blades, one moving sideways against the other, driven by a motor.
No safety data on specific models were available. A general reference notes blades need lubrication and that ceramic blades can break.

lead: BaByliss is a French personal care brand, now owned by the American group Conair, that sells hair dryers, curling irons, straighteners and, under its professional and men's lines, hair clippers and beard trimmers [1]. Within grooming discussions, its trimmers and stylers are one of several professional-style tool brands.
The sources available for this entry cover the company's history and general clipper technology; no published tests of BaByliss products or forum discussion were available.
infobox: France, marketed as BaByliss from July 1960

paras: According to Wikipedia, hairdressers René Lelièvre and Roger Lemoine in Montmartre invented the first electric hair straightener, which Jean-Pierre Feldblum marketed under the BaByliss name in July 1960. The company expanded across Western Europe, and Conair bought a majority share in February 1995. A professional line, BaBylissPRO, and a men's grooming line launched in 2003 followed [1].

A general reference explains that clippers use two comb-like blades, one sliding sideways against the other, to cut hair with a scissor-like action, and that motors are of magnetic, rotary or pivot types. Low blade friction, kept up by lubrication, is described as important, and ceramic blades resist corrosion but are brittle [2].
